about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Nydia M. Velázquez

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMBATING FOREIGN THREATS TO MAIN STREET ACT OF 2026
statements.title: COMBATING FOREIGN THREATS TO MAIN STREET ACT OF 2026
sentences: It will mandate the creation of an educational resource for small businesses on foreign adversary conduct harming them, and how to avoid and respond to such conduct.
I support sending this measure to the Senate so it gets the consideration and scrutiny that it deserves.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESHORING AMERICAN MANUFACTURING ACT OF 2026
statements.title: RESHORING AMERICAN MANUFACTURING ACT OF 2026
sentences: To that end, I recognize the importance of a strong domestic manufacturing sector and reliable supply chains.

That is why I supported the CHIPS and Science Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, which provided incentives for domestic semiconductor manufacturing, tax incentives for clean energy manufacturing, and investments in domestic materials, infrastructure, and supply chains.

Unfortunately, the current administration curtailed or eliminated several of these incentives, instead prioritizing tariff policies that have weakened the economy, slowed job growth, and put enormous strain on Main Street businesses.

Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 10375, the 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act, as amended.

statements.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WISDOM FOR INNOVATIVE SMALL ENTERPRISES ACT
sentences: AI outputs are prone to bias, discrimination, misinformation, and omissions.
The AI-WISE Act will direct SBA to create online AI literacy resources for entrepreneurs, so they have the tools to make sound choices on AI adoption and use.
Madam Speaker, I am proud to support H.R. 5784, the AI-WISE Act.
Madam Speaker, I commend Ms. Scholten and Mr. Downing for their dedication to our Nation's innovative small enterprises, and I urge my colleagues to support H.R. 5784.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REMOVAL OF THE USE OF UNITED STATES FORCES FOR HOSTILITIES WITHIN OR AGAINST VENEZUELA
statements.title: REMOVAL OF THE USE OF UNITED STATES FORCES FOR HOSTILITIES WITHIN OR AGAINST VENEZUELA
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of this War Powers Resolution.
Twenty-three years ago, I stood on this same floor as Congress debated an Authorization for Use of Military Force in Iraq.
This is about regime change and control of Venezuela's resources.
Nicolas Maduro is a dictator, and you don't have to defend him to recognize a simple truth: Venezuela does not pose an imminent threat, and a war will do nothing to make America safer.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support this resolution.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SMALL BUSINESS REGULATORY REDUCTION ACT OF 2025
statements.title: SMALL BUSINESS REGULATORY REDUCTION ACT OF 2025
sentences: Let me begin by stating that I wish we were here to talk about bills to help small businesses grow or policies that address challenges they are facing today, like tariffs and the cost of groceries and healthcare.
Inflation, tariffs, and finding good employees are some of the top challenges facing small businesses.

Take a walk down a Main Street, Mr. Speaker, and you will hear the same concern from small business owners up and down the block: The uncertainty and rising costs tied to the President Trump tariffs are crushing their small businesses, plain and simple.
Mr. Speaker, I will close with this: Trump's tariffs, not regulations, are crushing small businesses.
I know that it is painful for the other side of the aisle to discuss or even debate the issue of tariffs and how it is negatively impacting small businesses.
Witnesses have testified before our committee that the costs of tariffs are harming their small businesses.
I know they don't want to talk about tariffs and, instead, we are debating these two bills.

The American Action Forum estimates that Trump's tariffs are costing small businesses $85 billion a year, and that is not including the cost of navigating the uncertain environment or complying with the tariffs themselves.
The tariffs disproportionately harm small firms, which operate on thinner margins and have virtually no buying power.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to H.R. 2965, the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act.
For these reasons, I oppose the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act, and I urge my colleagues to oppose it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DESTROYING UNNECESSARY, MISALIGNED, AND PROHIBITIVE RED TAPE ACT
statements.title: DESTROYING UNNECESSARY, MISALIGNED, AND PROHIBITIVE RED TAPE ACT
sentences: They could have easily been about tariffs or unpaid invoices to contractors.
Mr. Speaker, small businesses are being crushed by the Trump tariffs, and the SBA Office of Advocacy, to the best of my knowledge, has not conveyed their concerns to the White House.

The Office of Advocacy is supposed to be an independent office within the SBA, and it is responsible for advancing the views and concerns of small businesses before Congress, the White House, Federal agencies, the Federal courts, and State and local policymakers, but it has done nothing on tariffs.
Instead of helping small businesses that are being crushed by the Trump tariffs, the majority is focused on creating another deregulatory hotline, even though one already exists on regulations.gov.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to H.R. 4305, the Destroying Unnecessary, Misaligned, and Prohibitive Red Tape Act, or the DUMP Red Tape Act.
For these reasons, I oppose the bill.
I urge my colleagues to oppose the bill and focus on real solutions to lift up small businesses during these troubling economic times.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EXTENSION OF SBIR AND STTR AUTHORITY
statements.title: EXTENSION OF SBIR AND STTR AUTHORITY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 5100, a simple bill to extend the Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer programs for an additional year.
We will continue to be at the table, ready to negotiate and ultimately pass a bipartisan, bicameral comprehensive reauthorization.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025
statements.title: DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025
sentences: It is ironic we are debating a bill called the CLARITY Act when it offers no clarity on one of the biggest issues in crypto, the blatant conflicts of interest inside our own government.
Foreign investors, some under Federal investigation, are pouring millions into these ventures, buying access, influence, and favorable treatment.

With this bill, not only are we continuing to allow President Trump to issue his cryptocurrency, but we are allowing him and his cronies to be in charge of the regulators overseeing that venture and compromising the stability of capital markets in our country.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to this bill.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no.''

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GUIDING AND ESTABLISHING NATIONAL INNOVATION FOR U.S. STABLECOINS ACT
statements.title: GUIDING AND ESTABLISHING NATIONAL INNOVATION FOR U.S. STABLECOINS ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in opposition to the GENIUS Act.
From the beginning, I have said that Congress needs to tackle stablecoin legislation, but we cannot pretend that this is happening in a vacuum.
We are creating a framework for stablecoins while the President, his family, and members of his administration are personally invested in this market and directly profiting from it.
Now, his family firm, World Liberty Financial, has launched its own stablecoin, once again netting the President's family tens of millions of dollars.
It doesn't bar the President or Cabinet officials from holding financial stakes in stablecoin issuers.
It doesn't address the foreign investors piling into these ventures.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no.''

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICAN ENTREPRENEURS FIRST ACT OF 2025
statements.title: AMERICAN ENTREPRENEURS FIRST ACT OF 2025
sentences: If we really wanted to put American entrepreneurs first, we would be debating a bill to strengthen SBA lending and make it easier to access capital, or we could stop playing political games and finally vote to exempt small businesses from these painful on-again, off-again tariffs.
Unfortunately, this bill does nothing to help small businesses grow or adjust to supply chain disruptions or unexpected tariff costs.
Secondly, there is no evidence, not a shred of evidence, that has been shared with Members of Congress, the public, the IG, or other law enforcement officials.
If we are being asked to enact such drastic measures without proper vetting or a thoughtful process, then we need more than her assurances.
What they call an illegal may actually be a visa holder, a green card holder, or someone with DACA or TPS protections.
Without a full accounting of this case, we could be looking at an illegal rescission of loan funds made by the Trump administration.

Those rules required 51 percent ownership of a business by a citizen or permanent resident, meaning a 49 percent ownership stake by a short- term resident, like a DACA recipient, was permissible if other requirements were met.

On that note, if they have identified this as fraud or abuse, then there is a process in place to turn over these findings to the Office of Inspector General and other law enforcement for a full investigation.
I don't disagree, but I remind my colleagues that some of the individuals they refer to as ``illegals,'' which in many cases means people with TPS or DACA status, do pay taxes.
They contribute to Social Security.
Businesses could be shut out of SBA lending because of a foreign investor with less than 2 percent ownership.
There is no evidence that undocumented immigrants are getting loans they are not supposed to.
It targets small business owners who are here legally, people like DACA recipients, visa holders, and refugees; people who are building businesses, creating jobs, and following every rule.
It forces them to track and verify the age and citizenship status of every single businessowner down to the last percentage point.
Tariffs are driving up the costs of goods.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to H.R. 2966, the American Entrepreneurs First Act.

My colleagues across the aisle keep claiming that the Administrator, along with DOGE, identified a case wherein an illegal alien--we will get to my thoughts on that term in a minute--received a nearly $1 million loan despite holding only 49 percent ownership of a business.
I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this bill and focus instead on solutions that will truly help American small businesses.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAVE SBA FROM SANCTUARY CITIES ACT OF 2025
statements.title: SAVE SBA FROM SANCTUARY CITIES ACT OF 2025
sentences: It strips regional, district, and local SBA offices out of so- called sanctuary cities, despite there being no legal definition and no justification for such a move.
Let's not forget, entrepreneurs across the country are already dealing with higher prices caused by tariffs.
Just maybe, my colleagues could stop playing games and pass a bill exempting small businesses from the pain of this administration's on- again, off-again tariffs.

Mr. Speaker, I insert into the Record two news articles about DHS sanctuary jurisdiction lists removed from their website given the fact that their local sheriffs were opposed to the lists, as well as a Third Way article highlighting that the red State murder rate was 33 percent higher than the blue State murder rate, which can be found at: https://www.thirdway.org/report/the-21st- century-red-state-murder-crisis.
We respectfully urge you to oppose the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act, H.R. 2931.
The Save SBA from Sanctuary CMes Act is a blatant attempt to coerce cities into abandoning their values and violating the Constitution in service of Trump's unpopular, unlawful deportation agenda.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong opposition to H.R. 2931.
I urge my colleagues to reject this bill, stand up for small business owners in every ZIP Code and restore the SBA mission as a nonpartisan advocate for America's entrepreneurs.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CAPPING EXCESSIVE AWARDING OF SBLC ENTRANTS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: CAPPING EXCESSIVE AWARDING OF SBLC ENTRANTS ACT OF 2025
sentences: At a time when small businesses are facing rising costs, tariff uncertainty, and tightening credit, Congress should be doing everything it can to expand access to capital, not pulling back on programs that are actually working.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to H.R. 2987, the so- called Capping Excessive Awarding of SBLC Entrants Act, or the CEASE Act.

While I understand and share some of the concerns raised about how the SBA has handled oversight of these licenses, I cannot support legislation that is rushed, vague, and potentially harmful to the very businesses we are supposed to be helping.
That is a goal that I support.
That is why I cannot support this bill in its current form.

In sum, I oppose H.R. 2987 because it will not protect the Community Advantage program, which has a solid track record of providing smaller dollar loans to thousands of women, veterans, rural, and underserved entrepreneurs.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WOSB ACCOUNTABILITY ACT
statements.title: WOSB ACCOUNTABILITY ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I urge all Members to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FULL-YEAR CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2025
statements.title: FULL-YEAR CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2025
sentences: This bill slashes $23 billion from veterans' benefits, turning its back on the brave men and women who served our country; guts healthcare, leaving families, children, and seniors vulnerable; and it slashes affordable housing, putting thousands, including veterans, domestic violence survivors, and people with disabilities at risk of losing their homes.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to this reckless Republican funding bill.
I will not vote for a CR that green lights these dangerous cuts.
Democrats are ready to fund the government, but we will not stand by while Republicans sell out the people we are sworn to serve.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to reject this dangerous bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONCURRENT RESOLUTION ON THE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
statements.title: CONCURRENT RESOLUTION ON THE BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025
sentences: This budget slashes $880 billion from Medicaid, putting 286,000 people in my district, including nearly 100,000 children, at risk of losing healthcare.
All this to hand out trillions of dollars in tax breaks to the top 1 percent.
Instead, it made the rich richer while working people fell further behind.
Now they are doubling down, making America sicker, poorer, and hungrier just to funnel more money to their billionaire donors.
This isn't fiscal responsibility.
Madam Chair, I rise today in strong opposition to this Republican rip-off.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ASSISTING SMALL BUSINESSES NOT FRAUDSTERS ACT
statements.title: ASSISTING SMALL BUSINESSES NOT FRAUDSTERS ACT
sentences: Whether it is a neighborhood childcare center, or a bakery on Main Street, they are creating neighborhood jobs and reinvesting in the local economies.
I have been particularly troubled by the pauses in Federal funding to small businesses, inflationary tariffs, and Elon Musk's access to the SBA's HR, contract, and payment systems.
